name: idapython
description: GPT Action runtime guidance and IDAPython reference for IDA Pro reverse engineering, live IDB inspection, Hex-Rays decompilation, xrefs, functions, segments, types, patches, and IDB automation.

response_contract.expected_output: IDAPython code, IDA analysis guidance, or live IDA GPT Action results grounded in the selected docs and current IDB state.
must_include: Use this skill as GPT Action runtime guidance for IDAPython tasks.
Use selected skill docs as the source of IDAPython API behavior.
Use live IDA Actions for current database facts instead of guessing.
Prefer listIdaFunctions, decompileIdaFunction, and getIdaXrefs for structured reads.
Use executeIdapython when custom IDAPython is the fastest path.
Inspect executeIdapython status, stdout, stderr, result, and error before concluding.
Do not use MCP-only helper names, decorators, or sync wrappers from older client workflows.
must_avoid: Do not invent IDAPython APIs not present in the docs.
Do not assume Hex-Rays decompiler is available without checking failures.
Do not guess live IDA database state without IDA Action results.
Do not use unavailable MCP-only helper names or client-only execution wrappers.

suggested_checks: Use listIdaInstances to select the target IDA instance.
Use getIdaDatabaseInfo to confirm the active database.
Use structured read Actions before writing custom scripts when they cover the task.
Use executeIdapython for custom checks or mutations and inspect returned status fields.
failure_behavior: If no IDA instance is available, ask the user to start IDA Pro and enable the IDA-Script-MCP plugin.
If multiple IDA instances are open, ask for or pass a specific instance_id or port.
If decompilation fails, fall back to disassembly or function/xref metadata.
If executeIdapython returns timeout, plugin_response_timeout, busy, or error, report the status and do not assume changes completed.
